claim_text: fscrypt operates at filesystem level and can protect different directory trees with distinct key domains.
qualification_or_note: Direct source characterization.

claim_text: fscrypt protects file contents and filenames for an offline point-in-time view, while most filesystem metadata remains visible.
qualification_or_note: Do not generalize to full metadata secrecy.

claim_text: fscrypt does not provide authenticity against an adversary that can modify encrypted storage while it is offline.
qualification_or_note: Direct source limitation.

claim_text: After an fscrypt key is installed, normal operating-system access controls govern access; privileged online compromise is outside its storage-at-rest boundary.
qualification_or_note: Inference phrased at source boundary, not a root-resistance claim.

claim_text: Removing an fscrypt master key does not immediately remove per-file keys for files still in use, including open files and certain active references.
qualification_or_note: Operationally material revocation caveat.

claim_text: Userspace must separately erase its own copies of fscrypt key material.
qualification_or_note: Direct source requirement.

claim_text: fscrypt key removal does not guarantee that every plaintext or key-derived copy in VFS caches, process memory, registers, or other layers has been erased.
qualification_or_note: No secure-wipe guarantee.

claim_text: fscrypt v2 policies are recommended over v1 for new deployments because v2 strengthens policy and key semantics.
qualification_or_note: Use kernel-supported current policy versions.

claim_text: The documented fscrypt modes do not provide authenticated encryption for file contents; ciphertext expansion and filesystem semantics are cited constraints.
qualification_or_note: Do not label fscrypt object-authenticating.

claim_text: LUKS2 is a generic key store for a volume key with multiple credentials/keyslots and extensible metadata.
qualification_or_note: Volume-key wrapping is distinct from object identity.

claim_text: LUKS2 header redundancy and checksums detect corruption but are not a general malicious-metadata authentication guarantee; metadata remains observable unless detached.
qualification_or_note: Do not conflate checksum with adversarial authenticity.

claim_text: Authenticated disk-encryption support through dm-crypt/dm-integrity is optional and documented as experimental in the selected stack.
qualification_or_note: Not the minimum portable baseline.

claim_text: LUKS2 reencryption has resilience modes with different crash-recovery behavior; partial or resilience-none operations carry explicit recovery risk.
qualification_or_note: Runbook must pin resilience and backup behavior.

claim_text: A LUKS header backup contains key material sufficient to unlock data with valid credentials and must be protected as sensitive key-bearing backup material.
qualification_or_note: Header backups participate in erasure and revocation analysis.

claim_text: Passing discard through an encrypted mapping can reveal allocation or filesystem-use patterns and has security implications.
qualification_or_note: Performance option, not deletion primitive.

claim_text: dm-integrity can store integrity tags and, when combined with dm-crypt authenticated modes, can convert detected tampering into I/O failure.
qualification_or_note: Block-level, not HaloKV principal binding.

claim_text: dm-integrity journal mode provides atomicity for data and integrity tags, while direct mode can expose tag/data mismatch after a crash.
qualification_or_note: Configuration materially affects recovery semantics.

claim_text: An unencrypted integrity journal may expose recent write patterns or data unless protected by the selected authenticated-encryption construction.
qualification_or_note: Residual leakage requires review.

claim_text: Closing a dm-crypt mapping removes the active mapping and key only when the mapping is no longer in use.
qualification_or_note: Unmount and drain first.

claim_text: Deferred close schedules mapping removal after the last user releases it rather than providing immediate revocation.
qualification_or_note: Deferred is availability-oriented, not instant key eviction.

claim_text: Erasing LUKS keyslots does not overwrite payload data, and an extant LUKS header backup can restore access.
qualification_or_note: All key-bearing copies must be considered.

claim_text: Changing a passphrase or keyslot wrapper is not the same operation as reencrypting payload data under a new volume key.
qualification_or_note: Separate credential rotation from data-key rotation.

claim_text: systemd crypttab configures encrypted block devices that are activated during boot.
qualification_or_note: Reference exact tagged source.

claim_text: systemd supports interactive, file, AF_UNIX, PKCS#11, FIDO2, and TPM2-related unlock mechanisms for encrypted volumes.
qualification_or_note: Mechanism choice does not by itself establish tenant identity.

claim_text: systemd password-agent infrastructure may temporarily cache interactively supplied passwords or PINs when configured to do so.
qualification_or_note: Disable or account for caching in threat model.

claim_text: A LUKS2 volume key linked into a kernel keyring is not automatically removed merely because the encrypted device is detached.
qualification_or_note: Explicit unlink/revoke lifecycle required.

claim_text: TPM2-bound unlock proves platform or policy state according to enrollment, not HaloKV tenant/project authority; principal binding remains an application control.
qualification_or_note: Human authority mapping remains open.

claim_text: Linux thread, process, session, user, and persistent keyrings have different possession and lifetime semantics; logon-type keys are not readable through normal userspace key-read APIs.
qualification_or_note: Kernel retention still requires lifecycle control.

claim_text: Kernel key revocation marks a key unusable for future operations but does not prove erasure of every derived or copied key.
qualification_or_note: Derived keys and active mappings are separate.

claim_text: GCM authenticates additional data without encrypting it and authenticated decryption returns plaintext or FAIL.
qualification_or_note: Foundation for fail-closed object handling.

claim_text: GCM IV uniqueness is a critical per-key requirement; reuse can compromise security.
qualification_or_note: Hard requirement.

claim_text: For the RBG-based GCM IV construction, the total invocations under a given key and supported IV length are bounded by 2^32.
qualification_or_note: Use stricter local limits where appropriate.

claim_text: A deterministic IV construction requires invocation-state preservation across power loss; inability to establish uniqueness requires a new key domain.
qualification_or_note: Epoch rollover is safer than guessing.

claim_text: An AEAD interface binds plaintext and associated data and returns an error on authentication failure.
qualification_or_note: Protocol-level framing reference.

claim_text: IETF ChaCha20-Poly1305 uses a 96-bit nonce that must be unique for each invocation with the same key.
qualification_or_note: Alternative AEAD suite.

claim_text: AES-GCM-SIV provides nonce-misuse resistance with explicit usage limits, but it does not make deliberate or unlimited nonce reuse acceptable.
qualification_or_note: Optional suite, not permission to ignore nonce state.

claim_text: HKDF uses extract-and-expand stages and an application-specific info field for context separation.
qualification_or_note: Suitable where HKDF is an approved implementation choice.

claim_text: SP 800-108 KDF constructions include Label and Context inputs intended to separate derived-key purposes and parties.
qualification_or_note: Encode canonical hierarchy context.

claim_text: XTS-AES is a confidentiality mode for storage devices and does not provide authentication.
qualification_or_note: Do not treat default LUKS XTS as integrity protection.

claim_text: Cryptographic keys move through defined lifecycle states, including pre-activation, active, deactivated, compromised, and destroyed states.
qualification_or_note: HaloKV epochs map to explicit state transitions.

claim_text: Logical deletion, overwrite commands, or discard are not automatically equivalent to verified media sanitization or cryptographic erase.
qualification_or_note: Technique must match media and policy.

claim_text: Cryptographic erase depends on rendering all relevant target-data encryption keys inaccessible, including copies, escrow, and hierarchical dependencies.
qualification_or_note: Scope is key-copy complete.

claim_text: Keys or plaintext may persist in volatile memory, processor registers, caches, or supporting systems and require separate handling.
qualification_or_note: CE is not a universal memory wipe.

claim_text: A sanitization program includes verification, validation, and documentation rather than relying only on command success.
qualification_or_note: Evidence trail is part of the procedure.

claim_text: Storage encryption technologies protect different layers and threat boundaries; full-disk, volume, file/folder, and virtual-disk controls are not interchangeable.
qualification_or_note: Use layered control selection.

claim_text: Cryptographic keys must be generated with approved random-bit-generation processes and sufficient strength for their intended algorithms.
qualification_or_note: No human-chosen data keys.

claim_text: HMAC is a keyed message-authentication construction suitable for scoped identifiers and manifest authentication when instantiated correctly.
qualification_or_note: Keyed identifier use is a synthesis decision.

claim_text: Argon2id is the primary Argon2 variant recommended by RFC 9106 for password hashing under its stated parameter profiles.
qualification_or_note: Use only when human memorized secrets are unavoidable.

claim_text: Deterministically encoded CBOR requires defined canonicalization choices so semantically identical data produces the same encoding.
qualification_or_note: Needed for stable AAD and identifiers.

claim_text: Object-level AEAD is mandatory for the minimum multi-user HaloKV persistent-cache profile; fscrypt and LUKS are defense-in-depth rather than substitutes.
qualification_or_note: Standards-backed synthesis.

claim_text: An unlocked LUKS volume is a host storage boundary, and fscrypt is a filesystem key-domain boundary; neither natively authenticates HaloKV tenant, project, prefix, rank, or object semantics.
qualification_or_note: Principal binding belongs in object AAD and authorization.

claim_text: Private content-addressed deduplication must be scoped no wider than the authorized tenant/project sharing domain.
qualification_or_note: Human-approved sharing policy sets the boundary.

claim_text: Public or system-prefix objects require a separate authority-owned namespace, signing/key policy, publication workflow, and read-only tenant consumption path.
qualification_or_note: Never silently promote private tenant objects into a global pool.

claim_text: Derive or wrap purpose-separated keys through canonical tenant/project/prefix/namespace/rank/epoch contexts, with separate encryption, identifier, manifest, and audit purposes.
qualification_or_note: Prevents cross-purpose and cross-domain key reuse.

claim_text: Each rank receives a separate AEAD key domain per epoch, or an equivalently rigorous nonce partition; uncertain nonce state forces a new epoch.
qualification_or_note: Simplifies local crash recovery and blast radius.

claim_text: Use HMAC-SHA-256 or another reviewed PRF under a scope-specific identifier key for private content identifiers; do not expose a global raw plaintext digest.
qualification_or_note: Still leaks equality within the authorized scope.

claim_text: Canonical AEAD associated data binds format version, suite, key epoch, authority, principal scope, prefix, namespace, sharing class, rank, object type, codec, sizes, chunk position, identifier, and manifest generation.
qualification_or_note: AAD fields remain visible unless separately encrypted.

claim_text: Any unknown, malformed, corrupt, unauthenticated, wrong-key, wrong-principal, wrong-rank, stale, or mismatched cache object produces one external result: MISS_RECOMPUTE.
qualification_or_note: No plaintext fallback or partial accept path.

claim_text: Authenticate the complete envelope and required AAD before decompression, deserialization, digest trust, manifest traversal, or exposure to a consumer.
qualification_or_note: Length limits are checked before allocation; authenticity before semantic use.

claim_text: AEAD authenticity alone does not prevent replay of an older valid object; enforce trusted epoch floors, manifest generations, or monotonic state where freshness matters.
qualification_or_note: Freshness is a separate control.

claim_text: Randomized AEAD ciphertext is not a stable cross-write deduplication key; deduplication should operate on a scoped authenticated identifier and then store one authorized ciphertext representation.
qualification_or_note: Do not deduplicate by global ciphertext equality.

claim_text: Encryption does not hide all sizes, access patterns, timing, allocation changes, or within-scope equality; cross-tenant timing isolation requires scheduling and lookup controls beyond cryptography.
qualification_or_note: Residual risk remains.

claim_text: On any cryptographic or format failure, delete or quarantine the suspect cache entry and recompute through the authoritative pipeline; never fall back to unauthenticated cached plaintext.
qualification_or_note: Availability impact is accepted over unsafe reuse.

claim_text: Do not back up regenerable cache content by default. If backup is required, treat ciphertext, manifests, format metadata, wrapped keys, header backups, and epoch state as one coherent protected set.
qualification_or_note: Backup policy is a human decision.

claim_text: Restore into a non-serving quarantine namespace, validate format and policy, unwrap only authorized epochs, authenticate every object or sample according to declared policy, and publish atomically only after acceptance.
qualification_or_note: No direct restore into live lookup path.

claim_text: Export decrypts only after authorization and authentication, then re-encrypts under an explicit destination authority and sharing scope; copying source ciphertext does not transfer principal authority.
qualification_or_note: Export is a new cryptographic context.

claim_text: Logical deletion removes indexes, manifests, serving references, and scheduled storage objects, but must not be described as physical sanitization or immediate byte erasure.
qualification_or_note: Record tombstone and retention effects.

claim_text: Per-object cryptographic erasure is supportable only when the object has an independently destroyable DEK or key-wrapping record and every usable copy and backup dependency is rendered inaccessible.
qualification_or_note: Shared epoch keys usually make erasure scope larger than one object.

claim_text: Keep discard disabled unless a documented performance decision accepts allocation leakage; enabling discard does not create a secure-deletion guarantee.
qualification_or_note: Separate performance and sanitization decisions.

claim_text: Following suspected key or nonce compromise, stop writes, establish a new epoch, revoke authorization, drain active users, invalidate affected manifests, quarantine suspect objects, and recompute or re-encrypt from trusted inputs.
qualification_or_note: Old ciphertext remains evidence, not serving data.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: fscrypt alone authenticates HaloKV objects or detects all offline tampering.
qualification_or_note: False for selected boundary.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: ordinary LUKS2/dm-crypt XTS provides per-object authenticity or tenant binding.
qualification_or_note: Confidentiality boundary only.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: unlink, overwrite, TRIM, discard, or filesystem free-space release is automatically secure deletion.
qualification_or_note: Media-dependent and unverified.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: key revocation instantly removes access from open files, active mappings, kernel keyrings, or processes.
qualification_or_note: Drain and memory lifecycle required.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: at-rest encryption protects plaintext from a compromised root account, kernel, hypervisor, DMA-capable actor, or authorized live process.
qualification_or_note: Outside selected control boundary.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: AEAD authentication by itself prevents rollback or replay of an older valid object.
qualification_or_note: Freshness state is separate.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: keyed content identifiers eliminate access-pattern, size, timing, or within-scope equality leakage.
qualification_or_note: They reduce public digest exposure only.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: cross-tenant global deduplication is privacy-neutral merely because payloads are encrypted.
qualification_or_note: Lookup and timing can form confirmation oracles.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: cryptographic erase is physical zeroization or proves all remanent media states are unrecoverable.
qualification_or_note: CE is key inaccessibility under stated assumptions.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: TPM-, FIDO2-, or PKCS#11-assisted volume unlock establishes HaloKV tenant/project principal authority.
qualification_or_note: It establishes a device/credential unlock condition.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: selecting a NIST-specified primitive automatically makes the HaloKV implementation FIPS validated, certified, or compliant.
qualification_or_note: Implementation/module/program status is separate.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: removing a LUKS keyslot is irreversible while header backups, alternate keyslots, escrow, or snapshots exist.
qualification_or_note: All unlock paths matter.

claim_text: Unsupported claim: an SSD or storage-provider discard acknowledgement proves physical cells have been sanitized.
qualification_or_note: Use media/provider-specific sanitize evidence and validation.
